newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain unions, employers to set final deal this week.
newsitem.headline: Spain unions, employers to set final deal this week.

text.p: Spain's unions and employers said on Monday they had almost put the finishing touches to a final accord on labour reforms and expected to announce an agreement later this week.
"The two sides are aiming to end negotiations on Monday and will meet with their respective committees on Tuesday," a spokeswoman from the Workers' Commissions union (CCOO) said.
The two sides said they could then announce a final deal on Wednesday or Thursday.
Unions and employers reached a preliminary agreement in March that provided the foundations for a final accord, and have been putting the agreement down on paper since then.
Labour Secretary Manuel Pimentel said on Monday the government intended to enforce the reforms before the summer.
"Our objective is to apply the new contract measures before summer...the principal problem is the various procedures required to pass the new labour reform," he told reporters.

The government hopes the reforms will go part of the way toward liberalising Spain's highly rigid labour market and suppressing its towering unemployment -- the highest in Europe at just under 22 percent.
The key feature of the accord is a permanent contract which allows for cheaper severance pay in cases of unfair dismissal -- 33 days per year worked with a maximum of 24 months.
However, clauses have been built in to ensure that existing permanent contracts with the old terms of 45 days per year worked with a maximum of 42 months, are not switched.
The accord also aims to clarify the reasons that an employer can give for redundancies. In the case of fair dismissals, an employer must only pay severance costs of 20 days per year worked.
Under the agreement a new National Employment Commission will be created, made up of union, employer and government representatives, responsible for following the progess of contracts.
